title: Clarify crediting and throttle behavior for async embeddings, rerank, and function-invocation pipelines
creator: Aisha Park
description: Background: We frequently see complex multi-stage non-chat pipelines where a single customer request triggers: (1) speculative/prefetch embedding calls, (2) fanout embeds -> rerank model(s), and (3) optional function/tool invocations or structured-output extractors. Current metering treats each of these stages as separate token and invocation events which leads to surprising charges when partial successes, retries, or idempotent replays occur. Goal: produce a clear, implementable spec that ensures predictable per-customer billing (no double-charge on retried operations), robust throttling behavior (fair backpressure across stages), and a reconciliation path for historical fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Billing, Runtime, and Platform teams
Implementation includes idempotency keys propagated across pipeline stages to avoid double-crediting
Throttle policy defined such that rate limits are applied both at per-endpoint and per-customer pipeline levels with documented priority rules
Reconciliation job implemented to detect and refund mis-attributed or duplicate charges for the last 90 days in staging and flagged for prod run
Prometheus metrics and Console dashboard created showing per-stage and end-to-end cost attribution and retry counts
E2E test harness validating partial success, speculative prefetch cancellation, and a retry loop without duplicated billing
technical_design: Overview: Introduce 'pipeline-level provenance' header carried through service boundaries (x-rw-pipeline-id + x-rw-stage-id + idempotency-key)

Dual-metering model: (A) token-meter records raw model tokens consumed per call; (B) invocation-credit-meter assigns a 1-time pipeline-level credit per logical customer request per configured granularity (per-rerank, per-embedding-fanout, per-toolcall). Reconciliation hooks translate token-meter rows to invoiceable units using pipeline provenance

Idempotency: Use a canonical idempotency key provided by SDK/Frontend or generated at ingress. All downstream services persist the idempotency key for 7 days and early-abort double processing if a completed record exists

Prefetch/cancellation semantics: Prefetched embeddings annotated as speculative and charged to a speculative bucket. If later promoted to canonical usage within 60s, promote charge; otherwise apply automated refund rules. Cancellation RPCs must include pipeline provenance to prevent orphaned charges
Retry handling: Retries with identical idempotency keys must be no-op at billing layer. Retries with different keys are treated as new requests unless linked via x-rw-replay-of header

Throttling policy: Implement two-tier throttles: global per-model rate limiter (existing) and pipeline-level concurrency quota to prevent runaway fanout. Priority rules: (1) critical toolcalls (customer tier 'enterprise') acquire capacity first, (2) otherwise fair-share based on customer committed capacity

Atomic checkpointing: At each stage, the billing service writes a checkpoint record with pipeline id, stage id, tokens consumed, invocation type, and state (pending|complete|aborted). Reconciliation uses these checkpoints to detect duplicates and missing refunds

Data model: Billing events emitted as immutable events to billing topic with pipeline provenance fields and idempotency key; downstream billing pipeline collapses events by (pipeline_id, logical_charge_type) before applying customer ledger updates

Monitoring: Add metrics: billing.pipeline_requests_total, billing.duplicate_attempts_total, billing.speculative_promotions_total, billing.refunds_processed_total; expose per-customer histograms for tokens-per-pipeline

Failure modes and mitigation: If checkpoint write fails, mark stage as 'tentative' and schedule compensating cleanup; limit retries with exponential backoff and circuit-breaker to avoid thundering-herd attribution spikes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy billing layer changes behind feature flag 'pipeline_billing_v2' with 100% staging traffic for two weeks
Phase 2 (internal): Enable for 5 internal customers/teams only. Monitor for discrepancies and reconcile with existing ledger
Phase 3 (beta): Open to selected external customers with explicit consent and visibility in Console billing preview
Phase 4 (full): Gradual 1%->100% traffic ramp with live reconciliation running in parallel and automated refunds queued for manual review before commit
Rollback: Feature flag off; reconciliation job identifies partial migrations and issues compensatory adjustments
test_plan: Unit tests: idempotency store behavior, speculative tag handling, checkpoint write semantics
Integration tests: end-to-end pipeline simulation with mocked model and tool backends validating no double-charge under N retries
Chaos tests: drop checkpoint writes and simulate partial stage commits to ensure reconciliation detects and repairs
Billing correctness suite: synthetic customers exercising edge cases (prefetch-only, partial-success, multi-tool fanout) with expected invoice lines
Load test: validates pipeline-level throttle prevents >X fanout per request at 95th percentile under burst
migration_steps: Back-compat: existing billing consumers will continue to process old events; new billing topic consumers run in parallel and write candidate ledger deltas to candidate table
Replay: write a one-time replay job to scan 90 days of events and emit collapsed pipeline-level charges for verification
Reconciliation: run reconciliation in dry-run mode for 2 weeks and surface candidate refunds in internal dashboard before applying to prod ledger
Customer notification: send opt-in emails to beta customers with detailed breakdown previews and support contact
Database migration: add pipeline_provenance indexes and idempotency stores with TTL
work_log: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Billing, and Platform. Attendees: Aisha Park, Miguel Santos, Riley Chen, Jordan Patel. Agreed goal and success metrics.
2026-02-18: Draft design posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILLING/Pipeline+Metering+V2. Feedback requested from Runtime and Legal.
2026-02-25: Runtime team requested clearer semantics for speculative-prefetch promotion window. Decided on 60s default with an env var to tune per-model.
2026-03-01: Prototype idempotency store implemented (redis-backed) and basic checkpoint write path coded. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284
2026-03-05: Billing observed a discrepancy in staging where speculative promotions were double-counted when toolchain retried concurrently. Added 'promotion lock' to gate promotion flow.
2026-03-10: Security/Privacy applied: ensured no PII in provenance headers. Security review concluded: no additional controls required for header propagation as long as TTLs are enforced.
2026-03-12: This ticket moved to In Progress; integration tests in CI failing intermittently on race between promotion and refund path. Investigating race conditions.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Chosen 60s speculative promotion window to balance latency vs. refund churn (decision by Runtime + Billing)
2026-03-05: Required idempotency keys be persisted for 7 days by all services to cover delayed retries and asynchronous tool callbacks
2026-03-10: Opted for dual-metering model (token-meter + invocation-credit-meter) to make invoicing simpler and preserve token visibility for performance teams

Complete reconciliation dry-run and surface candidate refunds in internal billing dashboard (assigned to Riley)
